title: NVLink error bisect notebook
content:
Goal: keep a step-by-step breadcrumbs log while I bisect a recurring GPU OOM that looks tied to NVLink/driver symbol mismatch. Put rough commands, error snippets, quick hypotheses, and minimal repro attempts here. This is a personal scratchpad — messy notes, TODOs, and experiments.

Summary of symptom:
- Intermittent OOM when launching multi-GPU inference container on 8x A100 (NVLink enabled). Works fine for small batches; fails when we enable peer-to-peer transfers + large KV cache.
- Errors rotate between: "CUDA driver: unknown error", "invalid device function", and noisy logs from nvidia-persistenced about symbol versions.
- Host nvidia-smi reports driver 525.85.12. Inside container, runtime/driver mismatch suspected (ldd/soname issues).

Repro notes (minimal):
- Command used to run failing job (k8s / dev node):
  docker run --rm --gpus all -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 -v /model:/model:ro --shm-size=1g redwood/infer:dev-20260310 
  python -u run_infer.py --model /model/llama-70b --batch 8 --use-kvcache --p2p

- Rapid failure (~10-30s) with large batches:
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "/app/run_infer.py", line 213, in <module>
      out = model.generate(batch)
  RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid device function

  Followed by kernel messages: 
  [ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID 21834: Ch 000000ff, PID 0, Class 0b, 200 0b, client 00000001, Reason: Xid 31, "SMU/DRM submission failed"

Diagnostics collected so far:
- Host checks:
  - nvidia-smi -q shows driver 525.85.12, cuda version 12.1 reported in nvidia-smi header.
  - /proc/driver/nvidia/version -> shows kernel module compiled with different gcc and older headers? (note: kernel module date 2025-11-03).
  - dmesg shows repeated "unrecognized symbol version" lines when container start (possible lib mismatch).

- Container checks:
  - ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so -> points to host-mounted libcuda.so (symlinked).
  - strings /usr/local/cuda/version.txt -> CUDA 11.8 (contradiction vs nvidia-smi).
  - nvidia-container-cli info returns: "[warning] libnvidia-container: incompatible libcuda versions found in container and host"

Commands run (dump):
- Collect host kernel/driver info:
  sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version > /tmp/driver.ver
  uname -a > /tmp/uname.txt
  sudo modinfo nvidia | egrep 'version|srcversion' > /tmp/nvidia-modinfo.txt
- Container introspection:
  docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint /bin/bash redwood/infer:dev-20260310 -c "ldd /app/_ext/torch_cuda.so || true; readelf -Ws /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so | head -n 20" > /tmp/ctr-ldd.txt
- Runtime tracing:
  strace -f -o /tmp/strace-python.txt -e trace=open,read,write,ioctl,poll python run_infer.py --small-repro
  nsenter -t <container_pid> -m -n -p cat /proc/<python_pid>/maps > /tmp/maps.txt

Observed oddities:
- libcuda.so inside container is a small shim (from older toolkit) that forwards to host libcuda, but symbol versions don't line up (libcuda.so.1 vs libcuda.so.460 vs libcuda.so.525 mismatch).
- Some kernels (cuBLAS/cuDNN) load fine but the P2P transfer setup fails when torch calls cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess — returns "invalid device function".
- Reproduces when both GPUs are linked via NVLink bridge; disabling NVLink (software side) avoids the crash.

Immediate hypotheses:
1) Kernel module (nvidia.ko) loaded on host was compiled against an older kernel or mismatched gcc, causing exported symbol versions to differ; userland runtime inside container expects newer versions. Result: subtle behavior when NVLink/P2P codepaths request newer symbols.
2) Mixed libcuda / libcudart in container vs host: container bundles CUDA 11.8 libs but host driver is for CUDA 12.x — symbol mismatch yields undefined behavior in certain codepaths (NVLink DMA, kernel launches).
3) A small microcode/firmware mismatch between the A100s after a recent reboot (one GPU has different firmware) causing P2P to fail in a way that surfaces as invalid device function rather than a clear driver error.
4) MPS / persistence daemon is clobbering contexts when multiple clients request P2P at the same time.

Next experiments to run (ordered):
- Quick isolation: reproduce on host without container: create a tiny cuda C repro that calls cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess on devices 0/1 with large allocations; compile with host cuda headers; run on host to see if same failure occurs. If it does, problem is host driver/module/firmware.
- Swap behavior: reboot node into alternate driver (if available) 515.x or 535.x and compare. Keep careful notes of kernel module timestamps.
- Force container to use host libs only (bind - mount /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* and /usr/local/nvidia into container) to eliminate dual-lib situations. Re-run repro.
- Check firmware with nvidia-smi --query-gpu=firmware_version --format=csv and cross-check across cards.
- Run small pyro reproducer under cuda-memcheck to catch invalid reads/writes if kernel launches are miscompiled.

Quick commands to capture canonical diagnostics (copy this block when filing issue):
- Host:
  sudo nvidia-smi -a > /tmp/nvidia-smi-a.txt
  sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version > /tmp/driver-version.txt
  sudo lsmod | grep nvidia > /tmp/nvidia-lsmod.txt
  sudo modinfo nvidia > /tmp/nvidia-modinfo-full.txt
  sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-tail.txt
- Container (immediately after failure):
  docker exec -it <ctr> bash -c "ldd $(python -c 'import torch; print(torch._C.__file__)')" > /tmp/ctr-torch-ldd.txt || true
  docker exec -it <ctr> bash -c "python -c 'import torch,sys; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.driver, torch.cuda.is_available())'" > /tmp/ctr-torch-versions.txt
  docker exec -it <ctr> bash -c "cat /usr/local/cuda/version.txt || true" > /tmp/ctr-cuda-version.txt

Notes on mitigations tried (and outcomes):
- Reboot node: temporary relief for ~12 hours, then error returns -> points to possible warm-state / workload pattern dependent bug.
- Downgraded container CUDA toolkit to 11.4: still fails with kernel Xid 31 (seems unrelated).
- Forced TORCH_USE_CUDA_DYNAMO=0 to avoid JITed kernels: no change.
- Disabled NVLink in runtime (soft disable by setting environment USE_P2P=0): avoids crash but performance regression.

Open TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Build and run minimal C repro on host (cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess + big allocs). Target: repro in < 2 min. Owner: Lena. Deadline: 2026-03-16.
- [ ] Collect firmware versions across rack + compare. Owner: Jordan.
- [ ] Try alternate driver 535.54.03 on staging node and run full inference harness. Owner: Amir.
- [ ] Attach perf trace / eBPF to observe where kernel-side hangs occur during P2P operations.

Notes for bug report (what to paste in ticket):
- Exact error text, host driver version, module build time, container CUDA runtime version, sample backtrace from dmesg (Xid entries), toy repro steps.
- Mention that disabling NVLink/P2P avoids failure — suggest P2P path in driver as likely suspect.

Misc tips remembered (for next time):
- If you see "unrecognized symbol version" in dmesg, it's almost always a kernel module / userland mismatch (recompile or align packages).
- libnvidia-container can hide mismatches by shimming; prefer not to ship mixed libcuda runtimes in containers if host driver isn't pinned.
- For quick local avoiders, set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to force synchronous errors (helps get precise location).

Appendix: tiny checklist for triage during incident call:
- Are all GPUs showing same firmware? nvidia-smi --query-gpu=firmware_version
- Are kernel module timestamps consistent across nodes? modinfo nvidia | grep -i 'compiled'
- Is container bundling a different libcudart/libcuda? ldd on torch._C and on libcuda in container
- Any recent driver/firmware upgrades in the rack? check ops change log

End of scratchpad. Keep appending quick commands/snippets as I run them.
